multicast.stream_profile: FIRST plus DATA packets with byte sequence space
multicast.go_back_n: receiver CNTL RSEQ selects rollback byte; sender resumes from containing segment
multicast.allocation_pacing: sender advances only within minimum receiver ALLOC after population discovery
multicast.reject_suppression: receiver multicasts reject notice and suppresses its own reject when an observed RSEQ is <= its required RSEQ
multicast.rate_control: sender honors minimum receiver RATE/BURST from CNTL; RATE=0xffffffff disables pacing

route_exchange.return_form: incoming ROUTE with high direction bit set
route_exchange.scope: endpoint ROUTE/XROUTE exchange; full multi-hop router forwarding remains separate

dev26_hardening.control_source_binding: unicast sender accepts a close-ACK only from the route destination: IPv4 address+port (udp), IPv4 address (raw36), destination MAC addressed to own MAC (l2). Source binding only; not authentication.
dev26_hardening.l2_destination_mac_enforced: unicast listener ignores frames not addressed to its own MAC
dev26_hardening.zero_throttle_fails_closed: operational_path_permitted is false and operational_delay_for_bytes is maximal when the effective rate is 0%, matching the planner CapacityGovernor; ooRexx XtpOperationalSocket returns -7
dev26_hardening.malformed_first_dropped: a FIRST with a malformed priority option, named-service segment or wire envelope is dropped unacknowledged (stderr XTP_DROP_MALFORMED); receive() keeps serving
dev26_hardening.decode_before_acknowledge: the wire envelope is decoded before the close-ACK, so an undecodable FIRST is never reported delivered
dev26_hardening.replay_scope: (peer host, KEY, FIRST payload digest): source MAC on l2, source IPv4 address on raw36/udp (port excluded so a restarted sender retrying the same KEY and payload is still suppressed); a colliding KEY with different bytes is delivered
not_addressed: send_message consulting the operational plan directly
dev26_hardening.control_return_bit_required: a close-ACK is accepted only if its KEY carries the XTP return bit

dev27_unicast_segmentation.single_packet_unchanged: a message plus its named-service segment that fits SendOptions::segment_bytes is one FIRST with EOM, byte-identical to dev26
dev27_unicast_segmentation.stream: larger messages are FIRST (no EOM) + DATA packets with byte SEQ, MULTI clear, SREQ on every packet; receiver must be dev27+
dev27_unicast_segmentation.segment_bytes_default: l2: interface MTU - 40; raw36 and udp: one maximal IP datagram (65472 / 65464 data bytes) so every message that worked before keeps the single-FIRST path
dev27_unicast_segmentation.flow_control: reuses the multicast go-back-N engine with one receiver: receiver ALLOC bounded by half the real socket receive buffer; RATE/BURST and operational capacityRate honoured
dev27_unicast_segmentation.retries: bound consecutive rounds without progress (streams only; multicast unchanged)
dev27_unicast_segmentation.receiver: reassembly per (peer host, KEY); service admission at FIRST; decode before the final close-ACK; up to 256 open streams; completed streams re-ACK a lost final close
dev27_unicast_segmentation.limitation: no selective retransmission (ECNTL/SPANS): under 20% forward / 14% reverse loss a 200-segment stream retransmitted 8867 packets

dev28_selective_retransmission.wire: XTP 3.4 CNTL NSPAN at control-segment offset +36 (always 0 before dev28) followed by NSPAN pairs [start,end) after the 40-byte control segment; DCHECK covers them; at most 64 spans
dev28_selective_retransmission.compatibility: an NSPAN=0 CNTL is byte-identical to dev27; dev26/dev27 parsers ignore spans; malformed NSPAN (overlong or inverted span) is refused
dev28_selective_retransmission.receiver: keeps out-of-order segments inside its advertised window and reports them as SPANs; a FIRST identical to one already seen is a retransmission: it no longer resets the stream, and after completion it only re-sends the close
dev28_selective_retransmission.sender: unicast streams use selective repeat: holes below the highest SPAN are resent after 2xSRTT; a receiver that never reports SPANs (dev27) gets go-back-N after three duplicate CNTLs; a full timeout resends everything unacknowledged inside ALLOC
dev28_selective_retransmission.measured: 200 segments through 20% forward / 14% reverse loss: 49 retransmissions (dev27: 8867)

dev29_sync_echo_diag.status_request: sender CNTL (KEY without the return bit), SYNC at control +20, SREQ in the trailer; dev28 and earlier receivers ignore it
dev29_sync_echo_diag.echo: receiver CNTLs carry ECHO at control +16 = the last SYNC received for that stream (0 until one arrives; byte-identical to dev28 when 0)
dev29_sync_echo_diag.context_binding: once the peer has echoed, the stream sender believes only CNTLs whose ECHO is a SYNC of this context (random 31-bit base per context); a stale or duplicated CNTL from another context with the same KEY is ignored
dev29_sync_echo_diag.exact_repair: the reply to SYNC k reflects every packet sent before k; any segment sent before k and still uncovered is resent at once
dev29_sync_echo_diag.wtimer: 2 x SYNC/ECHO round trip, floor 10 ms, doubling per consecutive timeout, cap 8 x timeout_ms; a peer that never echoes keeps fixed timeout_ms
dev29_sync_echo_diag.diag: packet type 8 (XTP 4.0 code), data CODE(4) VALUE(4) ASCII reason; code 1 CONTEXT_REFUSED with value 1 SERVICE_NOT_ADMITTED, 2 OVERSIZE, 3 MALFORMED; sent by the listener on refusal; every unicast sender fails fast on a DIAG that passes the same source and return-bit binding as an ACK
dev29_sync_echo_diag.measured: stale close injection: dev28 reports success without delivery, dev29 delivers; 100 KB at 20%/14% loss with timeout_ms=2000: dev28 2010 ms, dev29 7 ms; refused service: dev28 6.1 s, dev29 1 ms
dev29_sync_echo_diag.scope: SYNC/ECHO covers unicast streams; single-FIRST unicast and multicast are unchanged apart from DIAG
